ai.description: The Elongated Tortoise reaches 30 cm. Its carapace is oblong, yellow to olive with black blotches. It features a distinctively narrow, elongated shell and a yellow head with reddish eye markings.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Indotestudo elongata* is best identified by its elongated, yellowish-tan carapace with distinct black blotches, which contrasts with the darker, patterned shells of other Indian tortoises.
ai.habitat: The elongated tortoise inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests across South and Southeast Asia, typically found in leaf litter within low-altitude tropical regions.
ai.behavior: The Elongated Tortoise is primarily crepuscular, often emerging during dawn or dusk to forage for fallen fruits, mushrooms, and leafy vegetation in forest habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indotestudo elongata* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–6 eggs. In India, breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, peaking between July and November.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Elongated Tortoise occurs in Northeast India, primarily within the Brahmaputra Valley of Assam and parts of Tripura, inhabiting low-elevation forests and grasslands.
